Eurocopter AS350 Écureuil: France. The AS355 Ecureuil 2 is a twin-engine variant, marketed in North America as the TwinStar.
Who is credited with discovering Glutathione?
Glutathione: Frederick Hopkins. Glutathione (GSH,) is a tripeptide made of the amino acids glutamate, cysteine, and glycine.
Who is credited with discovering Blockchain?
Blockchain: Satoshi Nakamoto. A blockchain is a distributed ledger with growing lists of records (blocks) that are securely linked together via cryptographic hashes.
Who is credited with discovering Ethology?
Ethology: Isidore Geoffroy Saint-Hilaire. Ethology is a branch of zoology that studies the behaviour of non-human animals.

This British Formula One engineer, widely regarded as one of the sport's greatest designers, has served as technical chief at Williams, McLaren, and Red Bull, and now co-owns Aston Martin's F1 team — who is he?
Adrian Newey (born 26 December 1958) is a British engineer, aerodynamicist, automotive designer, and motorsport executive.
Endemic to the rainforests of Sumatra, this plant grows an enormous inflorescence that blooms only rarely and briefly, emitting the stench of rotting flesh to lure pollinators — what plant is it?
Amorphophallus titanum is a flowering plant in the family Araceae.
Coined by a French naturalist in 1799 from a Tupi word for the sound macaws make, this genus name covers eight species of long-tailed, brightly plumed Neotropical parrots — which genus?
Ara (bird) is a Neotropical genus of macaws with eight extant species and at least two extinct species.
One of the first grains ever domesticated, this cereal crop was cultivated in the Fertile Crescent around 9000 BC and later spread throughout Eurasia by 2000 BC — name the grain?
Barley (Hordeum vulgare), a member of the grass family, is a major cereal grain grown in temperate climates globally.
So dense that not even light can escape its gravity, this astronomical object's boundary of no return is called the event horizon — name it?
Black hole is an astronomical body so compact that its gravity prevents anything, including light, from escaping.
With a mass roughly 13 to 80 times Jupiter's, these substellar objects glow faintly from deuterium fusion rather than true hydrogen burning — what's the term for them?
Brown dwarf are substellar objects that have more mass than the biggest gas giant planets, but less than the least massive main-sequence stars.

Made of one oxygen atom triple-bonded to a single atom of the element that also forms diamonds and graphite, this colorless, odorless, poisonous gas is slightly less dense than air and typically arises from incomplete combustion — name the compound?
Carbon monoxide (chemical formula CO) is a poisonous, flammable gas that is colorless, odorless, tasteless, and slightly less dense than air.

Used to disinfect skin before surgery, sterilize surgical tools, treat oral yeast infections, and keep urinary catheters clear, this antiseptic compound comes as a gluconate or acetate salt — what is it?
Chlorhexidine is a disinfectant and antiseptic which is used for skin disinfection before surgery and to disinfect surgical instruments.
This bird group's rock-dove species gave rise to most domesticated pigeon breeds, including racing and fantail pigeons, and was later introduced to the Americas — which classification is it?
Columba (genus) comprises a genus of medium to large pigeons.
This bird family, the sole one in its taxonomic order, includes roadrunners, koels, malkohas, and coucals across roughly 150 species. Name the family?
Cuckoo are birds in the family Cuculidae, the sole taxon in the order Cuculiformes.

Occurring five times in the phrase 'no highway cowboys,' this linguistic term describes two vowel sounds gliding together within a single syllable, contrasting with a single steady vowel sound — what is it?
Diphthong (DIP-), also known as a gliding vowel or a vowel glide, is a combination of two adjacent vowel sounds within the same syllable.
Once hunted nearly to extinction for lamp oil, these true seals of the genus Mirounga are named for the male's large trunk-like snout, with males weighing up to 4,000 kilograms — which animal?
Elephant seal are very large, oceangoing true seals in the genus Mirounga.
Genus Vespa's largest eusocial wasp, this insect was introduced to North America as early as 1840 and remains the only true member of its genus found there — what is it?
European hornet (Vespa crabro) is the largest eusocial wasp native to Europe.
Holding doctorates in both medicine and philosophy from Pisa by age 21, this Italian naturalist became the "founder of experimental biology" by disproving spontaneous generation — who was he?
Francesco Redi (18 February 1626 - 1 March 1697) was an Italian physician, naturalist, biologist, and poet.
The most aggressive and common cancer to originate in the brain, this tumor is thought to arise from cells called astrocytes and carries a grim prognosis — what is it?
Glioblastoma (GBM), is the most aggressive and most common type of cancer that originates in the brain, and has a very poor prognosis for survival.
This Austrian physician wrote over 300 publications and termed his diagnosis of autism 'autistic psychopathy,' though later allegations tied him to a Nazi-era clinic in Vienna — what was his name?
Hans Asperger (18 February 1906 - 21 October 1980) was an Austrian physician.
Which cosmological relationship says a galaxy's recession speed is proportional to its distance from Earth, discovered via redshift measurements and usually credited to a 1929 paper?
Hubble's law is the observation in physical cosmology that galaxies are moving away from Earth at speeds proportional to their distance.
Usually caused by the Epstein–Barr virus and nicknamed 'glandular fever,' which illness brings fever, sore throat, swollen neck nodes, and a fatigue that can linger for months?
Infectious mononucleosis (IM, mono), also known as glandular fever, is an infection usually caused by the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV).

Called 'the greatest investor on Wall Street,' this founder of Renaissance Technologies made his fortune using mathematical models, after co-developing a key concept in differential geometry — who is he?
Jim Simons (April 25, 1938 - May 10, 2024) was an American hedge fund manager, investor, mathematician, and philanthropist.
Which German engineer and economist founded the World Economic Forum in 1971 and chaired it until stepping down in 2025?
Klaus Schwab (born 30 March 1938) is a German mechanical engineer, economist, and founder of the World Economic Forum (WEF).
This big-cat hybrid, born of a male lion and a female tiger, is the largest of all living cats, growing larger than either parent and enjoying a swim. What animal is it?
Liger is a hybrid offspring of a male lion (Panthera leo) and a tigress, or female tiger (Panthera tigris).

Developed by MathWorks, this proprietary programming language and numeric computing environment is built around matrix manipulation, and pairs with an add-on called Simulink for graphical simulation and model-based design. What software is this?
MATLAB (Matrix Laboratory) is a proprietary multi-paradigm programming language and numeric computing environment developed by MathWorks.
It's the science and practice of diagnosing, treating, and preventing disease — from pharmaceuticals and surgery to splints, psychotherapy, and ionizing radiation. What is this field?
Medicine is the science and practice of caring for patients, managing the diagnosis, prognosis, prevention, treatment and palliation of their injury or disease, while promoting their health.
Some of these tiny eight-legged arachnids live in soil as decomposers, others on plants causing galls, and one destructive parasite targets honeybee colonies — what are they?
Mite are small arachnids (eight-legged arthropods) of two large orders, the Acariformes and the Parasitiformes, which were historically grouped together in the subclass Acari.
This genus of spring-blooming perennials in the amaryllis family is better known by common names like daffodil and jonquil, with trumpet-shaped flowers usually white and yellow. What is it?
Narcissus (plant) is a genus of predominantly spring flowering perennial plants of the amaryllis family, Amaryllidaceae.
This family of three long, ribbon-like pelagic fish species includes the longest bony fish alive, stretching up to about 8 meters, yet rarely seen by humans — what fish is it?
Oarfish are the three species of large and extremely long pelagic lampriform fish belonging to the small family Regalecidae.

This genus of 70 to 100 frost-tolerant annual, biennial, and perennial species native to temperate Eurasia, Africa, and North America is the type genus of its flowering plant family — what's the genus?
Papaver is a genus of 70-100 species of frost-tolerant annuals, biennials, and perennials native to temperate and cold regions of Eurasia, Africa and North America.

This cellular process, in which a cell's outer membrane engulfs a large particle to form an internal compartment, is a key immune-system mechanism for clearing pathogens and cellular debris — what is it called?

Phagocytosis (from Ancient Greek (phagein) 'to eat' and (kytos) 'cell') is the process by which a cell uses its plasma membrane to engulf a large particle (0.5 m), giving rise to an internal compartment called the phagosome.
This radioactive, silvery-gray actinide metal with atomic number 94 forms oxides in moist air that can expand a sample by up to 70% in volume — which element?
Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
This thorny European shrub's tart fruit flavors a British gin, while its tough wood traditionally makes an Irish walking stick — what plant is it (scientific name)?
Prunus spinosa is a species of flowering plant in the rose family, Rosaceae.
First flown in 1955 as a nuclear-strike follow-on to the Mach 1 Super Sabre, this fighter-bomber earned the nickname 'Thud' and flew most early Vietnam War strike missions — which aircraft?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief is an American fighter-bomber that served with the United States Air Force from 1958 to 1984.
One of the world's oldest crops, this thistle-like annual plant with globular orange or red flower heads is grown commercially today for oil pressed from its seeds — what is it?
Safflower (Carthamus tinctorius), also false saffron, is a highly branched, herbaceous, thistle-like annual plant in the family Asteraceae.
Domesticated well over 3,000 years ago and grown widely in India, Myanmar, and Sudan today, this plant is considered one of the oldest oilseed crops known to humanity — what is it?
Sesame (Sesamum indicum) is a plant in the genus Sesamum, also called benne.
The largest of the toothed whales and the largest toothed predator alive, this pelagic giant has females who give birth only every four to twenty years — what is it?
Sperm whale (Physeter macrocephalus) is the largest of the toothed whales and the largest toothed predator.

Which British single-seat fighter plane, the only such aircraft Britain produced continuously throughout World War II, was famous for its innovative elliptical wing designed to be as thin as possible?
Supermarine Spitfire is a British single-seat fighter aircraft that was used by the Royal Air Force and other Allied countries before, during, and after World War II.
Raised by a wealthy uncle after his father fled following a fight, this English philosopher laid out an influential social contract theory in his 1651 book 'Leviathan' — who is he?

Thomas Hobbes (HOBZ; 5 April 1588 - 4 December 1679) was an English philosopher and political theorist, best known for his 1651 book Leviathan, in which he expounds an influential formulation of social contract theory.

These simple-looking marine invertebrates prove their kinship to vertebrates as larvae, when they sport a notochord, a dorsal nerve cord, and a post-anal tail — resembling a tiny tadpole. What are they?
Tunicate are marine invertebrates belonging to the subphylum Tunicata.
This canid genus contains the 'true foxes' — smaller and bushier-tailed than any wolf or jackal, typically living two to four years, occasionally a decade — which genus?
Vulpes is a genus of the subfamily Caninae.
Also known as AZT, this was the very first antiretroviral drug used against HIV/AIDS, and can be given during birth to prevent mother-to-child spread — what is it?
Zidovudine (ZDV), also known as azidothymidine (AZT), was the first antiretroviral medication used to prevent and treat HIV/AIDS.
This nucleoside, a building block of RNA, gives rise to the energy carriers ATP and ADP and is used as an intravenous drug for certain irregular heartbeats — what is it?
Working at a Soviet computing centre in 1985, this engineer designed one of history's most famous puzzle games — yet saw no royalties from it until founding a company around it in 1996. Who is he?
Domesticated in Southwest China roughly 2,000 years ago, this corm-producing plant is nicknamed 'devil's tongue' and gets boiled down into a jelly-like noodle called shirataki — what is it?
Amorphophallus konjac: Edible plant from Yunnan, China.
NATO codenamed 'Cub,' this four-engine Soviet turboprop served for three decades as the standard cargo and paratroop transport of the Soviet Air Forces — which aircraft?
Antonov An-12: Soviet medium-range transport aircraft.
Caused by the parasitic roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides and spread through food tainted with eggs, this infection most often hits children and is symptomless in over 85% of cases — what is it?
Ascariasis: Disease caused by the parasitic roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides. The eggs hatch in the intestines, the larvae burrow through the gut wall, and migrate to the lungs via the blood.
Native to the steppes of Central Asia, this two-humped pack animal's cold and drought tolerance made it indispensable to Silk Road caravans — what is it?
Bactrian camel: Species of mammal of Asia.
Known as silver birch for its peeling white bark, this deciduous tree native to Europe and Asia has become invasive in parts of North America — which species?
Betula pendula: Species of birch. Its range extends into Siberia, China, and southwest Asia in the mountains of northern Turkey, the Caucasus, and northern Iran.
After scrapping its Sonic Cruiser idea, this American planemaker launched an efficiency-focused wide-body in 2004 with a first order from All Nippon Airways — which aircraft?

Native to Europe, West Asia, and parts of North Africa, this widely introduced game fish is one of the world's worst invasive species outside its home range, with regional names like sewin in Wales and finnock in Scotland — which species is it?
Brown trout: Species of fish. Brown trout are highly adaptable and have evolved numerous ecotypes/subspecies.

Derived from an East Asian evergreen tree's wood, this waxy, strong-smelling terpenoid can also be synthesized from oil of turpentine and occurs in small amounts in rosemary leaves. What compound is it?
An obligate carnivore with retractable claws and crepuscular hunting habits, this small domesticated mammal communicates with everything from purrs and trills to hisses — what is it?
Cat: Small domesticated carnivorous mammal. The cat (Felis catus), also called domestic cat and house cat, is a small domesticated carnivorous mammal.

Convicted in 2013 for leaking nearly 750,000 classified documents to WikiLeaks while serving as an Army intelligence analyst in Iraq, this whistleblower had her sentence commuted by President Obama in 2017 — who is she?
Chelsea Manning: American activist and whistleblower (born 1987)
This inherited birth defect from a RUNX2 gene mutation leaves the collarbones underdeveloped or missing, letting the shoulders touch in front of the chest — which condition?
Cleidocranial dysostosis: Birth defect of the collarbones, skull, and teeth.
Declared one of the world's most invasive species in 2000 and named Australia's top pest problem in 2008, which highly adaptable Asian bird thrives in cities?
Common myna: Bird of the family Sturnidae.
Found mainly in muscle and brain tissue, which organic compound helps recycle ATP — its phosphorylated form donating phosphate to ADP to regenerate the body's energy currency?
Creatine: Chemical compound. Creatine ( or) is an organic compound that, in vertebrates, facilitates recycling of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), primarily in muscle and brain tissue.
Most genera in this family of armored, burrowing mammals are extinct — only one genus survives today, with eight living species — which family?

This widely used polar aprotic solvent dissolves both polar and nonpolar compounds, mixes with water, and — once absorbed through the skin — leaves a curious garlic-like taste in the mouth. Which organosulfur compound is it?
Dimethyl sulfoxide: Organosulfur chemical compound used as a solvent.

This movement disorder causes involuntary muscle contractions that twist the body into abnormal postures, and can sometimes be treated with botulinum toxin injections or deep brain stimulation — what is it?
Dystonia: Neurological movement disorder. Dystonia is often intensified or exacerbated by physical activity, and symptoms may progress into adjacent muscles.
Derived from Greek words for 'brain' and 'suffering,' this umbrella medical term covers any disease or disorder that causes overall brain dysfunction — what is it?
Encephalopathy: Disorders or diseases of the brain.
Combining five of mathematics' most fundamental constants — e, i, pi, 1, and 0 — into a single elegant equation, this formula is often called the most beautiful in mathematics. What is it?
Euler's identity: Mathematical equation linking e, i and π.
This subfamily of cats, distinguished by a bony hyoid that lets its members purr instead of roar, is informally known as the small cats — which subfamily?
Felinae: Subfamily of Felidae. The Felinae or small cats are a subfamily of the Felidae distinguished by a bony hyoid, because of which they can purr but not roar.

Present in about 80% of adults as harmless white or yellow bumps on the lips, cheeks, or gums, these visible sebaceous glands were first described in 1896 by an American dermatologist — what are they called?
Fordyce spots: Sebaceous glands that are present in most individuals.
Naming his most famous pistol after his 17th patent — not for holding seventeen rounds, as many assume — this Austrian engineer got his design into Austrian service in 1982 — who was he?
Prince Carl Philip, Duke of Värmland

The only Allied jet aircraft to see combat in World War II, this British fighter entered service with No. 616 Squadron RAF in July 1944, powered by engines pioneered by Frank Whittle — which aircraft?
Gloster Meteor: Britain's first jet fighter, 1943–1980s.

Native to the Amazon basin, this climbing plant's coffee-bean-sized seeds can be up to 6% caffeine — double a green coffee bean — making it a staple in Brazilian soft drinks and energy drinks — which plant?
Named for the Greek word for the sun, this element makes up about 24% of the universe's elemental mass and has the lowest boiling point of all — which colorless, odorless gas?
Helium: Chemical element with atomic number 2 (He)
German anthropologist Otto Schoetensack named this archaic human species in 1908 based on a jawbone found near the village of Mauer — then Europe's oldest known human fossil. Which species?

Homo heidelbergensis: Extinct species of archaic human. H. heidelbergensis has been regarded as either the last common ancestor of modern humans, Neanderthals, and Denisovans; or as a completely separate lineage.
A person with this condition becomes unduly alarmed by even the most minor symptom, convinced a serious illness is upon them despite no medical diagnosis — what is it?
Hypochondriasis: Excessive fear of developing illness.

This neurological emergency is sudden bleeding directly into brain tissue or its fluid-filled cavities — not from a blocked vessel, but a burst one — causing anything from headache to sudden paralysis. What is it?
Intracerebral hemorrhage: Type of intracranial bleeding that occurs within the brain tissue itself.
Enlisting disguised as a man named 'Jean' on Bougainville's expedition, this expert botanist became the first woman to circumnavigate the globe — who is she?
Jeanne Baret: French explorer, naturalist, botanist (1740–1807)
Personal physician to the Buddha and King Bimbisāra in 5th-century BCE Rājagṛha, this 'Medicine King' is still revered by traditional healers across Asia — who is he?

Jīvaka: Personal physician of the Buddha and Indian King Bimbisara. Jīvaka (Pali: Jīvaka Komārabhacca; Sanskrit: Jīvaka Kaumārabhṛtya) was the personal physician (Sanskrit: vaidya) of the Buddha and the Indian King Bimbisāra.
Named from Greek words for 'hare' and 'form,' this mammalian order splits into rabbits-and-hares on one branch and pikas on the other, totaling around 110 living species — which order?
Formed by cross-linking phenolic precursors, this class of complex organic polymers gives rigidity to plant cell walls, especially in wood and bark — what is it?
Lignin: Structural phenolic polymer in plant cell walls.
Native to Africa except for one species found only on Madagascar, this small parrot gets its common name from its strong, monogamous pair-bonding behavior — what is it?
This sexually dimorphic East Asian perching waterfowl, closely related to North America's wood-dwelling cousin, gets its species name from a Latin word for a wig — which bird?
Mandarin duck: Species of bird. The mandarin duck (Aix galericulata) is a perching duck species native to East and Northeast Asia.
This cone-shaped part of the brainstem controls involuntary functions from sneezing to heart rate, and was once known simply as 'the bulb' — which structure?
Medulla oblongata: Structure of the brain stem.
Named from Greek words for 'small' and 'head,' this congenital condition involves a smaller-than-average head size and can result from genetic syndromes or prenatal toxin exposure — what is it?
Microcephaly: Condition in which the head is small due to an underdeveloped brain.

Étienne Geoffroy split these simians into 'Old World' Catarrhini and 'New World' Platyrrhini groups, and counting them without the apes leaves a famously incomplete family tree — what common-name animal is this?
Monkey: Animal of the "higher primates", excluding apes.
This arthropod subphylum includes millipedes and centipedes, and one of its earliest fossils preserves the first known evidence of animals breathing air on land. What's the group called?
Myriapoda: Subphylum of arthropods. The group contains about 13,000 species, all of them terrestrial.
This small sauropod dinosaur had a wide muzzle packed with more than 500 teeth that were replaced roughly every two weeks — what genus is it?

This family of 138 primate species — including baboons, macaques, and mandrills — split off from a separate lineage of primates some 45 to 55 million years ago, yet is the closer kin to apes of the two — which family?
Old World monkey: Family of mammals. Old World monkey genera include baboons (genus Papio), red colobus (genus Piliocolobus), and macaques (genus Macaca).
Nicknamed 'forever chemicals' for their long environmental lifetimes, this class of synthetic compounds has been used in everything from Teflon to firefighting foam since 1938 — what's it called?
PFAS: Class of perfluorinated chemical compounds.
Often described simply as the act of teaching, this discipline studies how knowledge and skills are imparted — and how that process shapes learners socially and psychologically. What is it?
Pedagogy: Theory and practice of education.
This toxic gas, which smells like freshly cut hay, was responsible for tens of thousands of deaths as a chemical weapon in World War I — what is it?
Named after the American diplomat who introduced it from Mexico, this red-and-green Christmas plant is not actually toxic to pets — which plant?
Also known as face blindness, this cognitive disorder leaves a person unable to recognize familiar faces — even their own — while other visual skills stay intact. What is it?
Prosopagnosia: Cognitive disorder of face perception. Prosopagnosia should not be confused with prosopometamorphopsia, a disorder characterized by altered perceptions of faces.
Some specimens of this native European tree, whose acorns dangle on long stalks, are believed to be over 1,000 years old — name the species?
Quercus robur: Species of flowering plant.
Striking children recovering from a viral illness like the flu, this brain disease has been linked in about 90% of cases to aspirin use — what is it called?
Reye syndrome: Rapidly worsening brain disease.
Discovered in 1861 via flame spectroscopy by Bunsen and Kirchhoff, this alkali metal is named from the Latin word for 'deep red' — which element?
Rubidium: Chemical element with atomic number 37 (Rb)
Caused by the same Group A strep behind strep throat, this childhood illness brings a sandpapery red rash and a bumpy tongue — what is it?

Though crustaceans within this food category are more closely related to insects and spiders than to true fish, what group — including molluscs, crustaceans, and echinoderms — ranks among the most common food allergens?
Shellfish: Culinary and fisheries term for exoskeleton-bearing aquatic invertebrates.
Once called 'hyposulphite of soda,' this reducing agent treats cyanide poisoning and served as photography's key fixer in the 19th century — what compound?
Sodium thiosulfate: Chemical compound. Sodium thiosulfate (sodium thiosulphate) is an inorganic compound with the formula Na2S2O3·xH2O.

An English dyer and astronomer, he was the first to systematically show, around 1729, that electricity could travel through metals — flipping the era's focus from mere static sparks to conduction. Who was he?
Stephen Gray (scientist): English physicist. Stephen Gray (December 1666 – February 1736) was an English dyer and astronomer who was the first to systematically experiment with electrical conduction.
Commonly known as fainting, this fast-onset, short-duration loss of consciousness and muscle strength is typically caused by a sudden drop in blood flow to the brain — what's the medical term?
Syncope (medicine): Transient loss of consciousness and postural tone.
Also sold under the name dronabinol, this principal psychoactive compound in cannabis is prescribed to relieve chemotherapy-induced nausea and HIV/AIDS-related appetite loss — what is it?
Tetrahydrocannabinol: Psychoactive component of cannabis. It is the principal psychoactive constituent of Cannabis and one of at least 113 total cannabinoids identified on the plant.
Sitting between cells and organs in the body's organization, this assembly of similar cells and their extracellular matrix takes its English name from a French word meaning 'to weave' — what is it?
Tissue (biology): Group of similar cells performing a specific function.
Roughly three times stiffer than steel and nearly as hard as diamond, this gray powder is sintered into cutting tools, armor-piercing bullets, and jewelry — what compound is it?
Tungsten carbide: Hard, dense and stiff chemical compound.
The brightest star in the constellation Lyra, this star sits just 25 light-years away and served as Earth's northern pole star around 12,000 BCE — which star?
Vega: Brightest star in the constellation Lyra. It has the Bayer designation α Lyrae, which is Latinised to Alpha Lyrae and abbreviated Alpha Lyr or α Lyr.
With a distinctive pale eye and grey nape against black plumage, this small, gregarious member of the crow family was first formally described by Linnaeus — name the bird?
Western jackdaw: Species of bird in the crow family Corvidae.
Also called the pikeperch, this ray-finned game fish native to western Eurasian waters is the type species that gave its whole genus a name — which fish?
Zander: Species of fish. The zander (Sander lucioperca), sander or pikeperch, is a species of ray-finned fish from the family Percidae (which also includes perch, ruffe and darter).
What is the chemical symbol for sulfur?
The symbol for sulfur is S. Sulfur, also spelled as sulphur, is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.
What is the chemical symbol for rubidium?
The symbol for rubidium is Rb. Rubidium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rb and atomic number 37.

O. J. Simpson: Orenthal James Simpson (July 9, 1947 – April 10, 2024), nicknamed "the Juice", was an American football player, actor, and media personality.

James Dean: James Byron Dean (February 8, 1931 – September 30, 1955) was an American actor.

Kris Kristofferson: Kristoffer Kristofferson (June 22, 1936 – September 28, 2024) was an American musician, songwriter, and actor.

Ronald Reagan: Ronald Wilson Reagan (February 6, 1911 – June 5, 2004) was an American politician and actor who served as the 40th president of the United States from 1981 to 1989.
